messages:
Maria: P1 from tenant `stripe-ux` — p95 token latency spikes and occasional 500s on eu-west dedicated pool. Customer attached traces and says it happens during their midnight batch bursts.
Jun: Seen. Early suspicion: noisy neighbor within same host (MIG co-residency). Can we get node->slice assignments and a quick nvml snapshot?
Maria: Uploading allocation dump and a short request trace. Allocation: 
```
{"node":"gw-34-eu","slices":[{"tenant":"stripe-ux","mig":"1g.5g"},{"tenant":"other-batch","mig":"1g.1g"}],"time":"2026-03-15T00:12:13Z"}
```
InfraBot: Allocation snapshot saved to /var/log/support/alloc-dumps/2555551234.json 
Ali: That MIG mix (1g + 5g on same host) can be bad for small-gen workloads — L2 thrash and SM saturation across slices.
Jun: Can we reproduce quickly? Ask tenant to run our small generator: `redwood-load --profile=smallgen --qps=20 --model=redwood-1b --pool=eu-west-dedicated --slice=1g`
Maria: They ran it and saw p95 jump from ~120ms to ~700ms immediately, with bursts of 429s then 500s. Relevant log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T00:13:02Z] rpc_deadline_exceeded: call_id=3421
[2026-03-15T00:13:02Z] http 429 tenant=other-batch route=/generate
[2026-03-15T00:13:03Z] kernel warn: nvlink bw drop
```
Luis: Looks like SM saturation + memory pressure causing scheduler backoffs. Need NVML and nsys traces to confirm clocks and SM utilization.
Jun: Repro run to capture on-node: 
1) ssh node `ssh redwood@gw-34-eu`
2) collect nvml: `python /opt/redwood/tools/nvml_dump.py --duration 60 --out nvml-2555.json`
3) run `nsys profile -o repro -t cuda,osrt --sample=1s /opt/redwood/bin/serve-load --qps 20 --duration 60`
4) capture runtime logs `tail -n 500 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log`
Ali: Also run `nvidia-smi mig -lgi` and `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` to see L2/SM bursts. If L2 bandwidth spikes align with tenant batch start -> crosstalk.
Maria: I ran those commands on a repro node — MIG lists matched allocation dump. dmon shows repeated L2 bw spikes up to 70GB/s from slice belonging to other-batch.
Jun: Plan of action: 
- Collect NVML+nsys traces (Ali)
- Temporarily pin stripe-ux to a different host or enlarge slice (Maria)
- Apply short autoscale/burst policy tweak to increase capacity while we investigate (Ash can do)
- Long term: scheduler-level per-slice resource caps and per-tenant throttles
Ash: I can deploy a canary policy now: set `pool.eu-west-dedicated.autoscale.burst_limit=1.5` for tenant `stripe-ux` for 2h, will monitor.
Maria: Customer asked for repro artifacts and ETA for mitigation. I'll tell them 4h for initial NVML/nsys analysis.
InfraBot: Escalation created INC-2026, linked support ticket ST-23245, assignees: Ali, Jun.
Ali: I'll run the NVML+nsys reproducer on staging with identical MIG layout and post traces here. ETA ~4 hours.
Jun: If confirmed, short-term mitigations: migrate stripe-ux to its own host or change their reserved slice to a larger one (5g) to reduce cross-slice interference. Long-term: add slice-aware scheduling policies in runtime.
Maria: Noted — filing all steps and attaching logs to ST-23245. Thanks team. :rotating_light:
